stem:
Express vector \(\overrightarrow{AC}\) in terms of vectors \(\overrightarrow{AB}\) and \(\overrightarrow{CB}\) shown in the following figure.

[Figure: a triangle with vertex A at the lower left, B at the lower right and C at the top. Three directed segments are drawn - \(\overrightarrow{AC}\) from A up to C, \(\overrightarrow{CB}\) from C down to B, and \(\overrightarrow{AB}\) from A across to B.]
solution:
Using the triangle law of addition of vectors we can write
\(\overrightarrow{AC} + \overrightarrow{CB} = \overrightarrow{AB}\)
\(\therefore \overrightarrow{AC} = \overrightarrow{AB} - \overrightarrow{CB}\)
diagramNote: Fig. on printed p.19: triangle A-B-C carrying the three directed segments AC, CB and AB. The stem says 'shown in the following figure', so the sense of each arrow is given only there; it is described in the stem so the row is answerable without it.

stem:
From the following figure, determine the resultant of four forces \(\vec{A_1}, \vec{A_2}, \vec{A_3}\) and \(\vec{A_4}\).

[Figure: an open polygon O-A-B-C-D. \(\vec{A_1}\) runs from O to A along the base, \(\vec{A_2}\) from A up to B, \(\vec{A_3}\) from B to C, and \(\vec{A_4}\) from C to D. A fifth vector \(\vec{A_5}\) is drawn from O to D, closing the figure.]
solution:
Join \(\overrightarrow{OB}\) to complete \(\Delta\) OAB as shown in (a)
Now, \(\overrightarrow{OB} = \overrightarrow{OA} + \overrightarrow{AB} = \vec{A_1} + \vec{A_2}\)
Join \(\overrightarrow{OC}\) to complete triangle OBC as shown in (b).
Now, \(\overrightarrow{OC} = \overrightarrow{OB} + \overrightarrow{BC} = \vec{A_1} + \vec{A_2} + \vec{A_3}\)
From triangle OCD,
\(\overrightarrow{OD} = \vec{A_5} = \overrightarrow{OC} + \overrightarrow{CD} = \vec{A_1} + \vec{A_2} + \vec{A_3} + \vec{A_4}\)
Thus \(\overrightarrow{OD}\) is the resultant of the four vectors, \(\vec{A_1}, \vec{A_2}, \vec{A_3}\) and \(\vec{A_4}\), represented by \(\overrightarrow{OA}, \overrightarrow{AB}, \overrightarrow{BC}\) and \(\overrightarrow{CD}\), respectively.
diagramNote: Fig. on printed p.19, plus the solution's Fig. (a) and Fig. (b): open polygon O-A-B-C-D whose successive sides are A1..A4, with A5 = OD. The stem opens 'From the following figure', so the polygon's connectivity is given only there; it is described in the stem so the row is answerable without it.

stem: Water is flowing in a stream with velocity 5 km/hr in an easterly direction relative to the shore. Speed of a boat is relative to still water is 20 km/hr. If the boat enters the stream heading North, with what velocity will the boat actually travel?
solution:
[Textbook misprint: \(\tan^{-1}(0.25) = 14^{\circ}02'\), where the book prints \(14^{\circ}04'\). The magnitude, \(20.61\) km/hr, is correct.]

The resultant velocity \(\vec{R}\) of the boat can be obtained by adding the two velocities using \(\Delta\) OAB shown in the figure. Magnitude of the resultant velocity is calculated as follows:
\(R = \sqrt{20^{2} + 5^{2}}\)
\(= \sqrt{425} = 20.61\) km / hr
The direction of the resultant velocity is
\(= \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{5}{20}\right) = \tan^{-1}(0.25)\)
\(= 14^{\circ}04'\)
\(\therefore\) The velocity of the boat is 20.61 km/hr in a direction \(14^{\circ}04'\) east of north.
_note: Printed-solution arithmetic slip, NOT answer-affecting at the stated precision: \(\tan^{-1}(0.25) = 14.0362^{\circ} = 14^{\circ}02'\), whereas the book prints \(14^{\circ}04'\) (= 14.0667 degrees). The magnitude 20.61 km/hr is correct (\(\sqrt{425} = 20.6155\)). Transcribed as printed. The stem's 'Speed of a boat is relative to still water' reproduces the book's own wording, including its stray 'is'.

stem: Find a unit vector in the direction of the vector \(3\hat{i} + 4\hat{j}\)
solution:
Let \(\vec{V} = 3\hat{i} + 4\hat{j}\)
Magnitude of \(\vec{V} = |\vec{V}| = \sqrt{3^{2} + 4^{2}} = \sqrt{25} = 5\)
\(\vec{V} = \hat{\alpha}\,|\vec{V}|\), where \(\hat{\alpha}\) is a unit vector along \(\vec{V}\).
\(\hat{\alpha} = \dfrac{\vec{V}}{|\vec{V}|} = \dfrac{3}{5}\hat{i} + \dfrac{4}{5}\hat{j}\)

stem: Given \(\vec{a} = \hat{i} + 2\hat{j}\) and \(\vec{b} = 2\hat{i} + \hat{j}\), what are the magnitudes of the two vectors? Are these two vectors equal?
solution:
\(|\vec{a}| = \sqrt{1^{2} + 2^{2}} = \sqrt{5}\)
\(|\vec{b}| = \sqrt{2^{2} + 1^{2}} = \sqrt{5}\)
The magnitudes of \(\vec{a}\) and \(\vec{b}\) are equal. However, their corresponding components are not equal i.e., \(a_x \ne b_x\) and \(a_y \ne b_y\). Hence, the two vectors are not equal.
